newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher on Wall Street rise.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher on Wall Street rise.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Wednesday, helped by a late recovery on Wall Street, but the Ybourse's advance lost steam as the blue-chip CAC-40 index bumped into a resistance zone.
The index was up 21.54 points, or 0.94 percent, at 2,322.97 at 0945 GMT, while the CAC-40 January futures contract rose 20.50 points to 2,325.50. Resistance is seen at 2,325-30 points.
Brokers said investors are also feeling cautious ahead of two important U.S. indicators due out on Thursday and Friday, the December producer price index and unemployment rate.

Shares in Dassault Aviation and Dassault Electronique rallied 4.86 percent and 6.13 percent, respectively, on speculation about the impact on the companies of the restructuring of France's defence and aerospace industries.

The government moved forward in its plans to merge state-owned Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation by asking the privatisation commission on Tuesday to study the parities of the Aerospatiale-Dassault Aviation merger.
The newspaper La Tribune said Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation may team up with engineering group Alcatel Alsthom in a joint bid for defence electronics company Thomson-CSF.
Alcatel shares were up 1.93 percent at 422.80 francs. The company declined comment.
